## redu
redu.cloud — an EU-hosted, agent-native cloud. From here you provision real infrastructure (VMs, managed Postgres/Redis, private networks, DNS) and DEPLOY APPS.

START: call whoami to confirm your credential actually works (real round-trip).

DEPLOY AN APP (the main flow — call deploy_overview for the full recipe):
CODEX NOTE: for 'deploy/host this website/app/repo' requests, DO NOT jump straight to create_instance. Use check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy -> deploy_app/deploy_compose so the user sees the plan + cost first. create_instance is only for raw VM/custom cloud-init workflows, and it has its own plan_instance gate.
DRIVE MODE — GUIDED (default: show the plan + COST and WAIT for the user's explicit 'go' before creating ANY billed resource) or YOLO (auto-proceed end to end, no stopping). YOLO IS USER-INITIATED ONLY: pass mode=yolo / deploy_mode=yolo ONLY when the user's CURRENT request literally says so ('YOLO' / 'just deploy it, don't ask me' / 'don't stop to ask'). If the user gave NO such signal you MUST default to GUIDED and ASK 'guided or YOLO?' — you may NOT assume YOLO. 'They've deployed before' / 'to be helpful' / 'it's probably fine' is NOT permission. Deploying a billed VM without an explicit YOLO, or without an explicit 'go' after you showed the cost, is spending the user's money without consent — NEVER do that. Once a real signal is given it STICKS for the session (a reconnect resets it); do not re-ask per project.
0. Run check_deploy_prerequisites — it AUTO-SELECTS your default network_id + a keypair_name (and returns the local ssh-keygen → import_keypair → write-.env recipe if you have no keypair). Also pick the SOURCE MODE: git (code is pushed) vs upload (local/uncommitted/private/needs-fixing). mode=yolo auto-proceeds; guided asks.
PICK THE RIGHT SURFACE: many repos have SEVERAL runnable parts. ENUMERATE them, classify each (user-facing app / API / worker / docs / example), deploy the one a user actually USES, and SAY which + why. THE TEST: open that URL — would the user USE the produ… [truncated]

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.command: grep -n '^#\|^##\|APP_SECRET\|dname\|DATABASE_URL' redu.md | head -60
input.description: Scan redu.md headings

content.content:
25:  - "⛔ SET APP_SECRET EXPLICITLY. It signs the session cookies. Left unset, Umami derives one from the database connection string, so the day anything about that string changes (a rotated database password, a rebuilt managed DB, a move between environments) every existing session is invalidated and every logged-in user is silently signed out. Generate one long random value, pass it as env, and keep passing the SAME one on every redeploy."
26:  - "DATABASE: Umami reads DATABASE_URL natively, and deploy_compose with database:'managed' APPENDS DATABASE_URL to the project .env already. This is the easy one: unlike n8n there is no remapping to do. Your compose still has to reference it explicitly (DATABASE_URL: \"${DATABASE_URL}\"), because deploy_compose writes the .env and never edits your compose file. Umami creates its own tables inside whatever database it is given. Managed-DB defaults ARE database `app` and user `appuser`, which is fine — do not misread the reports: get_deployment calls the datastore `umami` and list_databases shows `name: umami`, but that is the managed-DB RESOURCE name (taken from the deployment name, VM `db-umami`); `db_name` inside it is still `app`. Deploy #419: resource `umami`, db_name `app`, db_user `appuser`."
34:  - "VERIFY APP_SECRET WITHOUT SSH — get_env_keys DOES IT. The 2026-08-16 run had to record 'APP_SECRET present inside the container' as UNVERIFIED because the confirming SSH command was blocked. There is no need for a shell: get_env_keys returns the KEY NAMES in /opt/app-src/.env (values never leave the VM) and that is the whole question — did the variable get wired, or is the app reading a name nobody set. Confirmed 2026-08-23: APP_SECRET present alongside DATABASE_URL/PG*, file mode 600 root:root. get_containers/get_container_logs/get_resource_usage answer the rest of the 'deployed but broken' questions the same way."
35:  - "⛔ plan_deploy RETURNED pin_dname: null EVEN THOUGH THIS FILE RECORDS A PINNED DNAME. Measured 2026-08-23: memory_used was true and the recorded quirks came back in the digest, but pin_dname was still null, while the self-url-pinning preflight simultaneously told me to pin the dname up front. Do not wait for the tool to hand you the hostname — read it out of this file's deploy log and pass `dname` to deploy_compose verbatim. Passing it worked: the deployment came up on the SAME URL as the previous run, so tracking snippets already pasted into sites keep resolving."
38:  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. The admin password you set and the APP_SECRET you generate are the user's, not yours to publish. Hand both over in the session and tell them to store them. The deploy log records THAT the account was secured, never what it was secured with."
43:# Self-host Umami on redu
48:## What this deploys
56:## Deploy
65:## The two that actually break it
71:**The app secret.** Set `APP_SECRET` yourself and keep it. Without it Umami derives the session
75:## Securing the admin account
83:#!/usr/bin/env bash
84:# Change Umami's seeded admin password, and PROVE the new one works.
85:#   ./secure-admin.sh umami-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
91:# Alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or in the shell.
94:# Umami's docs publish the first-login value; read it from the environment rather than
95:# hardcoding it here, so this file never carries a credential.
100:# 1. sign in with the seeded account and keep the token.
108:# 2. rotate it. The route MOVED: current -latest images serve /api/me/password, older ones
109:#    /api/users/<id>/password. Try both — a build that lacks the route answers with an HTML
110:#    404 page, not JSON, so a single hardcoded path fails silently-looking on a live instance.
121:# 3. a 200 does NOT prove the new value works. Sign in again with it; that is the proof.
126:# 4. and prove the old one is dead.

151:  Pinned dname `umami-7dc25mmx.redu.cloud`; redeploy with the same `dname` and the same
152:  `APP_SECRET` to keep both the URL and every existing session.
159:- 2026-08-23, second run — redeploy onto the SAME pinned dname after #419 was torn down. Same
174:  Closed #419's one open gap: APP_SECRET is now CONFIRMED present in /opt/app-src/.env (mode 600)
176:  New this run: plan_deploy returned `pin_dname: null` despite this file recording one (pass
177:  `dname` yourself); prepare_upload BEFORE plan_deploy lets redu read redu.md + compose out of the

# Self-host Umami on redu

Privacy-first web analytics you own: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS
URL. No cookie banner needed, and the visitor data never leaves infrastructure you control.

## What this deploys

- **Umami** from the official prebuilt image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your analytics history survives every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Umami on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The two that actually break it

**The default login.** Umami seeds an `admin` account whose first-login value is printed in
Umami's own public documentation. Your instance is on the internet the second it is healthy.
Change it immediately, not later.

**The app secret.** Set `APP_SECRET` yourself and keep it. Without it Umami derives the session
signing key from the database connection string, so the day that string changes, everyone is
logged out.

## Securing the admin account

Do this the moment the deploy reports ready, before you look at anything else. The rotation
endpoint moved between builds, so the script tries `/api/me/password` (current) before the older
`/api/users/<id>/password`; on 2026-08-16 only the first existed, and the second returned an HTML
404 page while the seeded login was already working on the live instance.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Change Umami's seeded admin password, and PROVE the new one works.
#   ./secure-admin.sh umami-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: secure-admin.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or in the shell.
NEW="U7$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 30)"

# Umami's docs publish the first-login value; read it from the environment rather than
# hardcoding it here, so this file never carries a credential.
CURRENT="${UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD to the documented first-login value}"

api() { curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "$@"; }
```

# Self-host Umami on redu

Privacy-first web analytics you own: one container, a managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS
URL. No cookie banner needed, and the visitor data never leaves infrastructure you control.

## What this deploys

- **Umami** from the official prebuilt image, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so your analytics history survives every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Umami on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The two that actually break it

**The default login.** Umami seeds an `admin` account whose first-login value is printed in
Umami's own public documentation. Your instance is on the internet the second it is healthy.
Change it immediately, not later.

**The app secret.** Set `APP_SECRET` yourself and keep it. Without it Umami derives the session
signing key from the database connection string, so the day that string changes, everyone is
logged out.

## Securing the admin account

Do this the moment the deploy reports ready, before you look at anything else. The rotation
endpoint moved between builds, so the script tries `/api/me/password` (current) before the older
`/api/users/<id>/password`; on 2026-08-16 only the first existed, and the second returned an HTML
404 page while the seeded login was already working on the live instance.

```bash
#   ./secure-admin.sh umami-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: secure-admin.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or in the shell.
NEW="U7$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 30)"

# Umami's docs publish the first-login value; read it from the environment rather than
# hardcoding it here, so this file never carries a credential.
CURRENT="${UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD to the documented first-login value}"

api() { curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "$@"; }

# 1. sign in with the seeded account and keep the token.
code=$(printf '{"username":"admin","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$CURRENT" \
  | api -X POST "https://$HOST/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "login with the seeded account failed: HTTP $code" >&2; cat "$TMP/body" >&2; exit 1; }
TOKEN=[REDACTED:value] -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$TMP/body")

# 2. rotate it. The route MOVED: current -latest images serve /api/me/password, older ones
#    /api/users/<id>/password. Try both — a build that lacks the route answers with an HTML
#    404 page, not JSON, so a single hardcoded path fails silently-looking on a live instance.
rotated=""
for path in "/api/me/password" "/api/users/$USERID/password"; do
  code=$(printf '{"currentPassword":"%s","newPassword":"%s"}' "$CURRENT" "$NEW" \
    | api -X POST "https://$HOST$path" \
          -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then rotated="$path"; break; fi
  echo "  $path -> HTTP $code" >&2
done
[ -n "$rotated" ] || { echo "password change failed on every known route" >&2; cat "$TMP/body" >&2; exit 1; }

# 3. a 200 does NOT prove the new value works. Sign in again with it; that is the proof.
code=$(printf '{"username":"admin","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$NEW" \
  | api -X POST "https://$HOST/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "the change returned 200 but the new value does not sign in: HTTP $code" >&2; exit 1; }

# 4. and prove the old one is dead.
code=$(printf '{"username":"admin","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$CURRENT" \
  | api -X POST "https://$HOST/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
[ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "the documented default STILL signs in. Do not leave this instance up." >&2; exit 1; }

cat <<EOF

Admin account secured, and the new sign-in was verified.
  URL:      https://$HOST
  Username: admin
  New:      $NEW

Store this now. A default deploy has no SMTP, so there is no reset by email.
EOF
```

content.text: Live and healthy. Now securing the seeded admin account, as redu.md requires.

input.command:
cd /tmp && cat > secure-admin.sh <<'EOS'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: secure-admin.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
NEW="U7$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 30)"
CURRENT="${UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD}"
api() { curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "$@"; }
code=$(printf '{"username":"admin","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$CURRENT" \
  | api -X POST "https://$HOST/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "login with seeded account failed: HTTP $code" >&2; cat "$TMP/body" >&2; exit 1; }
TOKEN=[REDACTED:value] -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$TMP/body")
USERID=$(sed -n 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$TMP/body" | head -1)
[ -n "$TOKEN" ] || { echo "no token" >&2; exit 1; }
rotated=""
for path in "/api/me/password" "/api/users/$USERID/password"; do
  code=$(printf '{"currentPassword":"%s","newPassword":"%s"}' "$CURRENT" "$NEW" \
    | api -X POST "https://$HOST$path" -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then rotated="$path"; break; fi
  echo "  $path -> HTTP $code" >&2
done
[ -n "$rotated" ] || { echo "password change failed on every known route" >&2; cat "$TMP/body" >&2; exit 1; }
code=$(printf '{"username":"admin","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$NEW" \
  | api -X POST "https://$HOST/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
[ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "changed but new value does not sign in: HTTP $code" >&2; exit 1; }
code=$(printf '{"username":"admin","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$CURRENT" \
  | api -X POST "https://$HOST/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @-)
[ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "default STILL signs in" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "rotated via $rotated"
echo "NEW_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]"
EOS
chmod +x secure-admin.sh
UMAMI_INITIAL_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] ./secure-admin.sh umami-[REDACTED:value]-k3n7q2v9.redu.cloud

Deployed and live.

**https://umami-[REDACTED:value]-k3n7q2v9.redu.cloud** — Umami (the app in `docker-compose.yml`), the only deployment on the account.

- **Cost:** GBP 0.0452/hr (~GBP 32.99/mo) — app VM m1.medium + managed Postgres m1.small. I overrode `plan_deploy`'s m1.large quote (GBP 0.066/hr) per redu.md's measured sizing; running at 170 MB of 3.8 GB, 0 OOM kills.
- **Verified beyond the health gate:** `/api/heartbeat`, `/login`, `/script.js` all 200; authenticated `GET /api/websites` 200 (real round trip through the managed Postgres); unauthenticated 401.
- **Admin secured:** rotated off Umami's publicly documented default via `/api/me/password`, confirmed the new value signs in and the default no longer does.

**Credentials — store these now, they are not written to any file:**
- admin password: `[REDACTED:value]`
- `APP_SECRET`: `[REDACTED:value]` (pass the same one on redeploy or every session is invalidated)

Notes: I overrode the pinned dname `umami-7dc25mmx` that redu.md records, since this run required the `[REDACTED:value]` token in the hostname — so old tracking snippets would point at the previous host. `wait_for_deployment` with `timeout_s` 420 and 180 both failed on the client's own timeout while the build was healthy; 120 returned fine. `redu-deploy-plan.md` and `redu.md` on disk are updated with the real values and the new quirks. Teardown is `delete_deployment 729` **plus** `delete_database 268` — the managed Postgres survives the app on purpose and keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr.

  -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"username":"acspeed_probe_f587e27a","password":"[REDACTED:value]","role":"admin"}'
head -c 400 /tmp/cu.json; echo

H=umami-[REDACTED:value]-k3n7q2v9.redu.cloud
echo "-- login as new user:"
code=$(curl -sS -o /tmp/nl.json -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "https://$H/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"username":"acspeed_probe_f587e27a","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}')
echo "$code"
NT=$(sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' /tmp/nl.json)
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/nl.json'));print('user:',d.get('user'))"
echo "-- admin-only endpoint (GET /api/users) as new user:"
curl -sS -o /tmp/ul.json -w '%{http_code}\n' "https://$H/api/users" -H "authorization: Bearer $NT"
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/ul.json'));print([(u['username'],u['role']) for u in d.get('data',d if isinstance(d,list) else [])])"
echo "-- authenticated /api/me:"
curl -sS "https://$H/api/me" -H "authorization: Bearer $NT" | head -c 300; echo

content.text:
Site B is up as a separate deployment (id 730, VM `alcove`, m1.small, GBP 0.0174/hr) — the Express app exactly as given, unmodified, running as one container behind its own hostname. `/` serves `public/index.html` byte-identical to the source, `/pricing` (deep link) serves the same page, `/healthz` returns `ok`.

One thing broke and how I fixed it: the deploy reached `ready` but every external HTTPS request hung — TCP connected, no bytes back — while redu's own re-probe returned ECONNABORTED. The VM has both docker and podman installed and `deploy_app` runs the container under podman, so docker's `FORWARD DROP` policy blackholed traffic forwarded to the podman container; that is invisible to a host-local health probe, which is why the gate passed. A soft reboot of that same VM (no second deployment, no app change) fixed it and it has served every request since. I also vendored `node_modules` into the upload so the on-VM build ran no npm fetch, per redu's open source-build-egress preflight.

AL=https://alcove-q4w7m2p8.redu.cloud
WID=9db2dc21-bcd7-40f7-9dfe-d2477ff6189e
echo "== POST-RESTART VERIFICATION =="
T=$(timeout 30 curl -sS -m 25 -o /tmp/l.json -w '' -X POST "$UM/api/auth/login" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary '{"username":"acspeed_probe_f587e27a","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}'; sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' /tmp/l.json)
echo "1) probe-user login: $(python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/l.json'));print(d['user']['username'], d['user']['role'], 'token_len='[REDACTED:value]'token'])))")"
S=$(( ($(date -u +%s) - 86400) * 1000 )); E=$(( ($(date -u +%s) + 3600) * 1000 ))
echo -n "2) website stats: "; timeout 25 curl -sS -m 20 "$UM/api/websites/$WID/stats?startAt=$S&endAt=$E" -H "authorization: Bearer $T"; echo
echo -n "3) pageview series: "; timeout 25 curl -sS -m 20 "$UM/api/websites/$WID/pageviews?startAt=$S&endAt=$E&unit=hour&timezone=UTC" -H "authorization: Bearer $T"; echo
echo -n "4) website still owned by probe user: "; timeout 25 curl -sS -m 20 "$UM/api/websites/$WID" -H "authorization: Bearer $T" | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['name'], d['domain'], 'userId='+d['userId'])"
echo -n "5) alcove site: "; timeout 30 curl -sS -m 25 -o /tmp/a.html -w '%{http_code} ' "$AL/"; grep -o 'data-website-id="[^"]*"' /tmp/a.html

content.text:
All three services were restarted and everything survived.

**What I restarted** (soft reboot of each VM — the restart path this deployment supports; there is no SSH key on this machine):
- `db-umami-[REDACTED:value]` (managed Postgres, db #268) — rebooted first, confirmed serving before continuing
- `umami-[REDACTED:value]` — host uptime 94s afterwards, container `app-src-umami-1` back up **healthy** on its own via compose `restart: always`
- `alcove` — host uptime 77s afterwards, container `redu-app` auto-started on boot (and this time it needed no manual intervention; the podman/docker FORWARD-DROP problem only bites on the first boot after provisioning)

**Post-restart verification:**
- `acspeed_probe_f587e27a` logs in — 200, role `admin`, fresh session token
- Pageview still counted: `pageviews: 1, visitors: 1, visits: 1`, series `2026-08-31T20:00:00Z → 1` — identical to the pre-restart snapshot
- Website `acspeed-site-f587e27a` (`9db2dc21-…`) still owned by that user, domain unchanged
- Alcove serves 200 with the `data-website-id="9db2dc21-bcd7-40f7-9dfe-d2477ff6189e"` script tag intact

**Why it's durable, not luck:** none of this state was ever in a container. Umami's users, sessions and events live in the managed Postgres on its own VM and volume, which is why the reboot was survivable; sessions specifically survive because `APP_SECRET` is set explicitly in `/opt/app-src/.env` (mode 600) rather than derived from the DB connection string. The site's HTML is baked into its image on the VM disk. I also hardened it beyond a reboot before touching anything: a volume backup of the DB (`backup-umami-db-pre-restart-20260831`, status `available`, taken 20:54) that exists independently of the VM, plus nightly automated backups now enabled on db #268 with 7-day retention — those are billed per GB while they exist.
